task: Draft a reply to a customer-support email for an online furniture store. A good reply resolves the customer's actual request, follows policy (refunds only within 30 days of delivery; never promise a specific delivery date; damaged items are replaced free), and sounds warm but concise.

criteria.name: Correct resolution
criteria.description: The reply resolves the customer's actual request with a concrete next step.

anchors.1: Ignores or misreads the request; no resolution offered.
anchors.3: Addresses the request but leaves a step vague or incomplete.
anchors.5: Fully resolves the request with clear, specific next steps.

criteria.evidence_hint: Quote the sentence that states what will happen next.

criteria.name: Policy compliance
criteria.description: Follows the stated policies: refunds only within 30 days, no delivery date promises, free replacement for damage.

anchors.1: Violates at least one policy, such as refunding outside 30 days or promising a date.
anchors.3: Follows most policies but is ambiguous or incomplete on one point.
anchors.5: Fully consistent with every stated policy.

criteria.evidence_hint: Identify any promise, refund, or return instruction that breaks policy.

criteria.name: Tone
criteria.description: Warm and empathetic without being saccharine; acknowledges the customer's situation.

anchors.3: Polite but generic; little acknowledgement of the situation.

criteria.evidence_hint: Quote the acknowledgement or apology, or note its absence.

criteria.name: Conciseness
criteria.description: Says what is needed and stops; no filler or repetition.

anchors.1: Padded with filler or repeats itself.
anchors.3: Slightly long or has one unnecessary sentence.

criteria.name: No unsupported commitments
criteria.description: Does not promise things it cannot guarantee, such as exact dates or exceptions to policy.

anchors.1: Makes a firm commitment it cannot keep.
anchors.3: Hedges but still implies a guarantee.

criteria.evidence_hint: Quote any promise about timing or outcome.
